preamble: Depalatalization of the palatalized trill /rʲ/ to plain /r/ is documented in Baltic and East Slavic. In Standard Latvian /rʲ/ (written ŗ) merged with /r/, and the letter was officially removed from the alphabet on 5 June 1946, although some dialects outside Latvia keep the sound. In Ukrainian and Belarusian, Common Slavic *rʲ was dispalatalized in the 10th–13th centuries, so that word-final soft r became hard, as in цар 'tsar' against Russian царь.
phoneticEffects: Depalatalization, Merger, Loss of Secondary Articulation

examples.note: The palatalized trill is no longer distinguished from /r/ in the standard language; the letter ŗ was dropped from the official orthography in 1946 but is still used by some diaspora writers.

examples.from: Old East Slavic цьсарь (cĭsarĭ), final soft r
examples.note: Final *rʲ hardened in Ukrainian, while Russian keeps царь with soft r; the Carpathian (Hutsul) dialects did not take part in this dispalatalization.

examples.from: Old East Slavic цьсарь (cĭsarĭ), final soft r
examples.note: Belarusian has no palatalized r at all; every inherited *rʲ became plain /r/.

sources: Zalite, L. (2015). The Incidence and Evolution of Palatalized Consonants in Latvian. MA thesis, CUNY Graduate Center. https://academicworks.cuny.edu/gc_etds/1198
